rationale: Conformity (high feature duplication rate) detects fake profiles hiding in dominant patterns. Homophily violation (high homophily) identifies feature-neighbor mismatches. Community (modularity) finds nodes misaligned with communities. Attr struct mismatch (feature-structure divergence) captures attribute-structural inconsistencies. These methods complement each other by addressing different anomaly types: conformity and attr_struct_mismatch target feature-space issues, homophily_violation focuses on local feature-neighbor mismatches, and community detects structural misalignment.

Banned tolokers likely hide behind template/minimal profiles (conformity: mean=0.81, p50=0.87, feature_dup_rate=0.489), showing the highest landmarker signal. Attribute-structure mismatch (p99=0.91) reveals divergence between feature and structural rankings, indicating cross-modal anomalies. Homophily violation (p99=0.84) captures feature-neighbor mismatch, exploiting the high homophily (0.7492) where violations become salient. Community adherence (p99=0.73) identifies workers who don't fit the strong modular structure (modularity=0.5194, 26 communities). Together these four paradigms cover complementary mechanisms: profile conformity, cross-modal divergence, feature-neighborhood mismatch, and structural non-conformity.

Conformity shows the strongest signal (mean=0.811, p99=0.969, high tail separation) and is directly applicable: feature_dup_rate=0.489 indicates banned workers likely hide behind template profiles, which the negative-reconstruction-residual mechanism specifically targets. Homophily_violation provides complementary evidence (mean=0.387, p99=0.841) despite overall homophily=0.749, capturing workers whose behavioral features diverge from their neighbors. Attr_struct_mismatch adds orthogonal power (mean=0.352, p99=0.914), detecting banned workers whose observable attributes rank differently from their structural roles. Community provides structural perspective (mean=0.255, p99=0.734) with 26 communities (modularity=0.52), catching workers who don't fit any community—a signal independent of feature-based detection. Together these four paradigms compose complementary views: template conformity, neighbor divergence, attribute-structure disagreement, and community misfit.

Banned tolokers are likely detected via three complementary mechanisms: (1) Conformity (mean 0.8111, p99 0.9686)—the exceptionally high scores combined with feature_dup_rate 0.489 suggest banned workers hide by adopting template profiles, camouflaging themselves in the crowd; (2) Attr_struct_mismatch (mean 0.3521, p99 0.9141)—strong tail separation indicates workers whose claimed profiles diverge from their actual collaboration structure, a hallmark of deceptive behavior; (3) Homophily_violation (mean 0.387, p99 0.841)—given high homophily (0.7492) and modularity (0.5194), tolokers whose features mismatch their neighbors' features stand out as genuine anomalies within their task communities. These three paradigms are complementary: conformity captures profile camouflage, attr_struct_mismatch captures consistency violations, and homophily_violation captures peer mismatch.

The ban decision in Toloka is made per worker from profile and task-performance statistics, so the target class is defined in the 10-dimensional attribute space, not by the graph's wiring. An edge here only means two workers touched the same task, which is incidental co-participation rather than endorsement or affiliation: with avg_degree = 88.28, density = 0.015 and clustering_coeff = 0.5329, almost every worker shares a task with a large, mixed set of honest workers, so 'who my neighbors are' carries little information about whether I was banned. That rules out the structure-led paradigms despite their applicability: community (modularity = 0.5194, 26 communities recovers task-pool groupings, not sanctioned workers), local_affinity and homophily_violation (homophily = 0.7492 with degree 88 means neighbor averages are heavily smoothed toward the global mean, so a low-affinity node is mostly a low-degree or off-pool node), and spectral, whose landmarker is the flattest of all probes (p90 = 0.2998, p99 = 0.5512). one_class is the direct statement of the ban mechanism: legitimate workers occupy a compact operating envelope of approval rate, speed, acceptance and activity, and a ban marks a worker who left that envelope, i.e. distance from the normal boundary in embedding space. reconstruction is the attribute-level complement: because the graph is dense and homophilous, the neighborhood aggregate approximates the platform-wide norm, so the residual measures how far a worker's own statistics sit from the population's expected profile, an independent estimator of the same 'outside normal operation' notion via a different objective. attr_struct_mismatch supplies the genuinely orthogonal cross-modal view and has the widest landmarker spread of any fast probe (std = 0.2454, p90 = 0.7175, p99 = 0.9141), which is the expected signature of a banned worker here: an ordinary-looking position in the co-work graph (they do get tasks, so structure hides them) paired with an off-distribution attribute ranking. I reject conformity even though feature_dup_rate = 0.489 clears its gate, on both domain and distributional grounds: bans follow measurable behaviour rather than camouflage behind minimal profiles, and its landmarker is left-skewed and compressed at the ceiling (mean 0.8111 above p50 = 0.8696 only by saturation, p50 to p99 spans 0.8696 to 0.9686), so it has no separated upper tail to rank with. density is rejected as degenerate: p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0 with mean 0.0023 means the kNN/LOF probe assigns essentially all nodes the same value in this dense regime and cannot produce a usable ordering, so its role is covered by one_class at the global scale instead.

The target is a worker-level property: a ban is earned by how a toloker behaves (approval rate, speed, task statistics, profile completeness), not by who they happen to sit next to. Edges here are co-assignment artifacts (two workers linked because a project handed them the same task), so the structure carries the platform's task-allocation pattern far more than it carries misconduct, and a banned worker's neighbors are mostly ordinary workers who drew the same batch. That is why I lead with one_class: with feature_dim = 10 of dense, continuous performance statistics (feature_sparsity 0.48, so the matrix is real-valued, not a sparse bag-of-words), the normal worker population occupies a compact performance envelope and abuse shows up as falling outside it, which is exactly the SVDD boundary assumption, and it does not require the neighborhood to be informative. reconstruction is the complementary global-attribute view: an autoencoder over the same 10 statistics with light neighborhood smoothing catches workers whose feature combination cannot be regenerated from the population pattern, and it degrades gracefully when the graph term is uninformative. attr_struct_mismatch supplies the one structural view worth keeping, and its landmarker is the most separated of the fast paradigms (std 0.245, p90 0.72, p99 0.91 against a p50 of 0.31), flagging workers whose performance profile disagrees with their co-task position. I excluded the purely neighborhood-agreement paradigms (local_affinity, homophily_violation, community, spectral) as a redundant cluster measuring the same co-assignment structure: at density 0.0150, avg_degree 88.3 and clustering_coeff 0.533 the graph is near-saturated, homophily 0.749 is high so violation scores are dominated by degree, and modularity 0.519 over 26 communities reflects the 13 projects rather than misconduct. density is degenerate here: its landmarker is dead (mean 0.0023, p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0), which is the expected kNN collapse in a graph this dense. conformity is saturated rather than discriminative (p50 0.870, mean 0.811, so most nodes already score near the ceiling); the feature_dup_rate of 0.489 comes from only 10 coarse profile dimensions colliding, not from template camouflage, and banned tolokers are extreme workers rather than hidden-in-the-crowd ones.

The target is workers banned by the platform, and a ban is a global verdict on a worker's profile and task-performance statistics, not a statement about who they sat next to. That domain fact drives the selection. Structurally this graph gives local views almost nothing to work with: an edge only means 'worked on the same task', avg_degree = 88.28 over 1,038,000 edges at density 0.015 with clustering_coeff = 0.533, so banned and legitimate tolokers are densely interleaved inside the same 13 project cliques. With homophily = 0.749 a banned worker's neighborhood is mostly normal workers doing the same task, so neighbor-contrast paradigms measure task membership rather than misconduct: local_affinity confirms this with a flat, unseparated landmarker (mean 0.230, p95 0.496, p99 0.697), and density is degenerate (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0, mean 0.0023) because in a graph this dense no node sits in a sparse embedding region. one_class is first because it is the only paradigm whose assumption matches how the label is generated: the 10 profile/performance attributes (feature_dim = 10) define a compact band of acceptable worker behaviour, and a ban means falling outside that band on approval rate, speed or answer quality. SVDD on graph embeddings tests exactly that global boundary and does not depend on the uninformative neighborhood contrast. attr_struct_mismatch is second and is the most strongly separated landmarker in the pack (std = 0.245, p90 = 0.718, p95 = 0.799, p99 = 0.914), the one distribution with a genuinely heavy upper tail. It also has a clean domain reading: a banned toloker is often structurally ordinary or even prolific (high task overlap, max_degree = 2138) while attributively off-band, and cross-modal rank divergence is precisely the node whose structure says 'busy regular' and whose attributes say otherwise. reconstruction is third as a sign-aligned attribute model: with feature_dim = 10 and feature_dup_rate = 0.489 the attribute matrix is template-dominated, so residual magnitude measures how far a worker's stats are from the pattern their peers predict, giving a learned complement to the geometric one_class boundary. I deliberately excluded conformity despite feature_dup_rate = 0.489 clearing its gate, on two grounds: its landmarker is saturated rather than separated (mean 0.811, p50 0.870, with the whole p90-p99 range compressed into 0.936-0.969), so it cannot discriminate a large banned population; and it is defined as the negated linear reconstruction residual, so composing it with one_class and reconstruction would fuse a signal with its own negation and cancel. I also dropped community despite modularity = 0.519 over 26 communities, since those communities track the 13 projects and banned workers participate in projects normally, and a ban-farm would be a dense in-community group rather than the community misfit that paradigm flags. homophily_violation and spectral were dropped as redundant with the retained attribute views while inheriting the same degree confound from avg_degree = 88.28. The three selected views are sign-consistent (all flag deviation from the normal worker pattern) and cover three distinct evidence channels: geometric boundary, cross-modal disagreement, and neighborhood-predictive attribute residual.

local_affinity shows the strongest empirical signal (mean 0.5035, p90 0.7585, p95 0.8013, p99 0.8825 with sharp upper-tail separation), matching fraud detection where bad actors deviate from peer behavior. The moderate homophily (0.4967) confirms normal nodes cluster with similar neighbors, which fraudsters break. attr_struct_mismatch provides a complementary second signal (p95 0.8098, p99 0.9158), detecting fraudsters whose handcrafted features diverge from their structural position in the multi-relational graph. spectral (p99 0.523) adds a distinct frequency-domain structural view, flagging irregular patterns in graph smoothness that neither neighbor-affinity nor attribute-structure capture. Excluded density (mean 0.0114, negligible separation) and community (mean 0.0663, weak modularity 0.2485) due to insufficient empirical support.

Two dominant complementary mechanisms dominate the evidence. attr_struct_mismatch shows the strongest signal (p99=0.9158), indicating fraudsters have attributes that diverge sharply from what their structural position would predict—fraud's hallmark on review platforms. local_affinity is nearly equally strong (p99=0.8825), indicating fraudsters have low feature agreement with neighbors. These are complementary: the first captures global cross-modal divergence (attributes vs. structure), the second captures local neighborhood incoherence. The moderate homophily (0.4967) supports neighborhood-based detection being viable, and the high average degree (736.5) ensures sufficient neighborhood signal. Weaker paradigms (density p99=0.0602, community p99=0.4041) lack sufficient evidence for this graph's fraud task.

local_affinity shows the strongest signal (p99=0.88, clear upper-tail separation from mean 0.50), aligning with fraud detection where bad actors diverge from benign neighbors in feature space; attr_struct_mismatch provides complementary evidence (p99=0.92) of divergence between user profiles and network topology, expected when accounts are fabricated or repurposed; spectral adds a global structure view (p99=0.52) to complement local and cross-modal mechanisms. The moderate homophily (0.4967) and high clustering (0.511) support local-agreement-based detection, while the 25-feature space and heterogeneity in edge types (product, rating, text similarity) justify attribute-structure mismatch. Density and community paradigms are weak (density mean 0.011, low modularity 0.25) and redundant with these three.

The domain says fraud here is camouflaged: the three merged relations (U-P-U, U-S-U, U-V-U) are behavioural co-occurrence links, and U-S-U in particular (same star rating within one week) connects almost everyone to almost everyone. The profile confirms this, density = 0.123336, avg_degree = 736.5 with degree_std = 891.3 and max_degree = 6991, clustering_coeff = 0.511, modularity = 0.2485 over only 7 communities, is_power_law = false. In a graph this saturated, a fraudulent user is structurally indistinguishable from a benign one by construction, so paradigms that ask whether a node sits oddly in the graph (community adherence at modularity 0.2485, spectral high-frequency response, kNN density) have little to bite on. The density landmarker shows exactly that degeneracy: mean 0.0114 with p50 0.0076 and p99 0.0602, all scores collapsed into a narrow band because every node has hundreds of near neighbours. Community and spectral are similarly compressed around their medians (0.0436 and 0.1481). What does carry signal is the 25 handcrafted per-user behavioural features (feature_dim = 25, feature_sparsity = 0.4156, feature_dup_rate = 0.1762), which encode review conduct directly and are the quantity the helpful-vote criterion is a proxy for. attr_struct_mismatch is the primary choice because it is the exact operationalisation of camouflage, a user whose attribute ranking and structure ranking disagree, and its landmarker is the only one with a genuinely separated upper tail, p50 = 0.3381 rising to p90 = 0.7402, p95 = 0.8098, p99 = 0.9158 with std = 0.2531, so the mechanism is measurably present rather than assumed. one_class is the complementary attribute-side view: with only 25 dense behavioural dimensions the benign majority (the >80% helpful-vote population) forms a compact region, and fraudulent conduct shows up as distance from that centre without ever consulting the untrustworthy adjacency. reconstruction adds a third, jointly attribute-and-structure view, an autoencoder over 25 features that flags users whose profile cannot be regenerated from the crowd they blend into; it overlaps partially with the first two but reads the attributes through the graph rather than beside it. I deliberately drop local_affinity and homophily_violation despite homophily = 0.4967 clearing their thresholds: at 736 neighbours per node, neighbour averaging regresses every node to the global mean (local_affinity mean 0.5035 sits on top of p50 0.5288), and camouflage is precisely the strategy of keeping neighbour agreement high, so these two would be actively misled rather than merely weak.

The target is defined by per-user review behaviour (helpful-vote ratio), and the 25 handcrafted features are exactly per-user behavioural statistics, so the discriminative signal sits in attribute space rather than in the wiring. The wiring itself is close to uninformative here: density 0.123 with avg_degree 736.5 on 11944 nodes and 8.8M edges is a consequence of how the three relations are merged (U-S-U links any two users sharing a star rating inside a week, U-P-U any two users touching the same product), so a 'neighbourhood' is a large arbitrary slice of the platform. Averaging over ~736 such neighbours pulls every node toward the global mean, which is visible in the landmarkers: homophily_violation (mean 0.150, std 0.092, p50 0.143, p90 0.232) and spectral (mean 0.152, std 0.088, p90 0.211) are collapsed with no separated upper tail, and modularity 0.2485 over 7 communities says the partition is too weak to carry a community-residual signal. Neighbour-agreement views are also the ones review fraudsters defeat by design: camouflage means wiring into benign users while behaving abnormally, so homophily 0.4967 overstates how much a neighbour tells you. one_class leads because it draws a boundary around the normal behavioural envelope without needing neighbour agreement, which matches a task where fraudulent users are those whose review statistics fall outside what an established helpful reviewer looks like; feature_dim 25 with feature_sparsity 0.4156 is a compact dense space where an SVDD boundary is well posed. attr_struct_mismatch is the sharpest landmarker on offer (mean 0.370, std 0.253, p90 0.740, p95 0.810, p99 0.916), a wide well separated tail, and it is the one paradigm that turns camouflage into evidence rather than noise: structure says ordinary, attributes say otherwise. density adds a local view that one_class cannot give, flagging users who sit off the manifold of their behavioural peers rather than far from a single global centre; its tail is separated in relative terms (p50 0.0076, p95 0.0299, p99 0.0602, roughly 8x the median). I dropped reconstruction, community and spectral because degree_std 891.3 exceeds avg_degree 736.5, so structure-driven scores on this graph mostly re-rank by degree, and I dropped local_affinity and homophily_violation as redundant with each other and blunted by both the neighbourhood dilution and the camouflage described above.

The task label is a global per-user property (share of helpful votes), not a neighborhood property, and this graph destroys every neighborhood-relative reference: density = 0.1233 with avg_degree = 736.5 and max_degree = 6991 means an average ego-net is a large, near-random slice of the 11944 nodes, so any neighbor mean converges to the global mean. The U-S-U relation (same star rating within a week) and U-V-U (top 5% TF-IDF similarity) are cheap, near-automatic edges, which is exactly how the 8.8M edges arise and exactly how a fraudulent reviewer ends up structurally indistinguishable from benign users. That is camouflage, so I favour paradigms that read the 25 handcrafted behavioral features globally, plus one that explicitly measures attribute/structure disagreement. (1) one_class: SVDD draws a compact boundary around the dominant benign behavior profile in a 25-d handcrafted feature space (feature_dim = 25, feature_sparsity = 0.4156), which matches a definition of fraud as global behavioral deviation rather than local disagreement, and it needs no local reference. (2) attr_struct_mismatch: the best-separated landmarker here, p50 = 0.3381 jumping to p90 = 0.7402 and p99 = 0.9158 with std = 0.2531, so the mechanism is genuinely present, and it is the direct operationalization of camouflage (structure ranks a user as ordinary, the handcrafted attributes do not). (3) density: a sharply isolated tail, p99 = 0.0602 against p50 = 0.0076 (roughly 8x) with mean = 0.0114, so a small minority really does sit in sparse embedding regions; LOF/kNN is non-parametric and catches deviants that fall outside the single SVDD ball, which the parametric boundary would miss if benign behavior is multi-modal (feature_dup_rate = 0.1762 hints at repeated profile clusters). (4) reconstruction: an attribute autoencoder over 25 dense handcrafted features gives a fourth, differently-parameterized view of feature-space typicality and covers the case where fraudulent profiles are reproducible in structure but not in attributes. Deliberately excluded: local_affinity, homophily_violation and contrastive all assume a meaningful local reference that avg_degree = 736.5 washes out, and local_affinity's landmarker confirms it with a smooth, diffuse ramp (mean = 0.5035, p90 = 0.7585, p95 = 0.8013, p99 = 0.8825) showing no separated tail; community is undermined by modularity = 0.2485 over only 7 communities (weak partition, so 'fits no community' is ill-defined); spectral high-frequency response is unreliable at this density with spectral_gap = 2.6912; adversarial adds a noisy, high-variance view without a distinct assumption from the reconstruction one already selected.

Contrastive (cross-view agreement) leverages the multi-relational graph structure to detect anomalies in cross-view inconsistencies. Homophily violation targets feature-neighbor mismatches in a high-homophily graph, capturing potential fraud signals. Attr-struct mismatch identifies divergence between attribute-based and structure-based rankings, complementing the other two by addressing cross-modal discrepancies. These three paradigms are complementary and supported by strong upper-tail distributions (p99 > 0.5) in the FAST-PARADIGM scores.
